# Just Eat API
Just Eat offers services for our various business partners and our consumer applications.
How you interact with the API depends on the services you wish to interact with.
## Security
### HTTPS
All api calls and callbacks require HTTPS. Your service will need a valid SSL certificate and be accessible via the standard SSL port (port 443).
## Making an API request
Some API calls require an API key, to authenticate the partner calling the API.
```
PUT https://uk-partnerapi.just-eat.io/orders/abcd1234 HTTP/1.1
Authorization: JE-API-KEY abcd123456789
```
Other calls require a user token in the form of a JWT.
```
GET https://uk.api.just-eat.io/consumer/me/orders/uk HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer abcd123456789
```

## Date Formats
### Date and time formats
All dates and times should use the [ISO 8601 standard for representation of dates and times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).

#### For instance:
* DueDateWithUtcOffset: `"2015-05-26T14:52:35.5444292+01:00"`
  - Local time: `14:52`
  - UTC time: `13:52`
  - UTC offset: `+1hr` (due to daylight time saving)
* DueDateWithUtcOffset: `"2015-02-03T11:10:00.0000000+00:00"`
  - Local time: `11:10`
  - UTC time: `11:10`
  - UTC offset: `0` (no daylight time saving, local time is equivalent to UTC)

Note that the offset may be for a timezone different to your own, so you should alway convert to your own local time for display purposes (e.g. on receipts and terminals).

### Callback timestamps
Timestamps sent to Just Eat should be recorded as the current local time (including any changes needed to account for daylight saving) with an accompanying offset that shows the difference between the recorded local time and the current UTC time.

If it is not possible to record timestamps in local time, timestamps may be recorded in UTC time with a 00:00 offset.
## Async Webhooks
Some of the webhooks on the platform are configured as being 'async' webhooks. These are for long-running operations, and work as follows:
  1. Your webhook is invoked with a `?callback={returnUrl}` query string parameter. The `returnUrl` is a unique URL that you will need to send the async response to.
  2. Return an immediate `202 Accepted` response from the webhook endpoint, to indicate that you have received the request.
  3. Perform the long-running operation. This can be deemed either a _success_; or a _failure_.
  4. If the result is a _**success**_, return the following:
  ```
  POST {returnUrl} HTTP/1.1

  {
        "status": "Success",
        "message": "{successMessage}",
        "data": {}   // webhook-specific response object
  }
  ```
  5. Otherwise, if the result is a _**failure**_, return the following:
  ```
  POST {returnUrl} HTTP/1.1

  {
        "status": "Failure",
        "message": "{failureMessage}",
        "data": {}   // webhook-specific response object
  }
  ```

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://uk.api.just-eat.io">https://uk.api.just-eat.io</a> - Production URL for the UK API

* <a href="https://i18n.api.just-eat.io">https://i18n.api.just-eat.io</a> - Production URL for the DK, ES, IE, IT and NO API

* <a href="https://aus.api.just-eat.io">https://aus.api.just-eat.io</a> - Production URL for the AU and NZ API

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Bearer token authentication using a JSON Web Token (JWT).

* API Key (api_key)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header. APIs for delivery partners require an API key that will have been issued to you.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic A few services allow the use of basic authentication when a partner doesn't support OAuth based authentication.

- OpenID Connect authentication. ADFS authentication provider for internal Just Eat tools.

    - OpenID Connect URL = [https://adfs.just-eat.com/adfs/.well-known/openid-configuration](https://adfs.just-eat.com/adfs/.well-known/openid-configuration)

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Bearer token authentication using a JSON Web Token (JWT), used by the restaurant sign up system

<h1 id="just-eat-uk-checkout">Checkout</h1>

## Get Checkout

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/checkout/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'User-Agent: string'
```

`GET /checkout/{tenant}/{checkoutId}`

Get the details required to fulfil an order, which includes:
  - The restaurant selling the items to be purchased
  - The customer making the purchase
  - How, where and when the items will be received by the customer
  - Instructions about the order


<h3 id="get-checkout-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Update Checkout

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/checkout/string/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -d '[
    {
      "op": "add",
      "path": "/customer",
      "value": {
        "dateOfBirth": "1980-01-30",
        "phoneNumber": "+447111111111"
      }
    }
  ]'
```

`PATCH /checkout/{tenant}/{checkoutId}`

Update the details required to fulfil an order, which includes:
  - The customer making the purchase
  - Where and when the items will be received by the customer
  - Instructions about the order


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "op": "add",
    "path": "/customer",
    "value": {
      "dateOfBirth": "1980-01-30",
      "phoneNumber": "+447111111111"
    }
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-checkout-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|A two-character country code. <br><br>The following countries are supported:<br>  - United Kingdom (UK)<br>  - Australia (AU)<br>  - New Zealand (NZ)<br>|
|checkoutId|path|string|true|A unique identifier for a checkout. This is currently a Basket Id.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|Allows the server to identify the application making the request.|
|body|body|[CheckoutUpdateRequest](#schemacheckoutupdaterequest)|true|none|
|» customer|body|object \| null|false|Details of the customer making the purchase.|
|» » dateOfBirth|body|string \| null|false|Customer's date of birth represented in ISO 8601 format. If a time is submitted, it will be ignored.<br><br>Required in Australia (AU) and New Zealand (NZ) only for fulfilling an order that contain items being purchased that require age verification.<br>|
|» » firstName|body|string \| null|false|Customer's first name. <br><br>Also known as Given Name(s).<br>|
|» » lastName|body|string \| null|false|Customer's last name (Optional). <br><br>Also known as Family Name.<br>|
|» » phoneNumber|body|string \| null|false|Customer's phone number.<br><br>A phone number can be represented in:<br>  - E.164 format e.g. +447777111111 or;<br>  - Local format of submitted tenant e.g. 07777111111.<br><br>E.164 formatted phone numbers are preferred.<br>|
|» fulfilment|body|object \| null|false|How and when the items will be received by the customer.|
|» » location|body|object \| null|false|The destination the customer wants to receive the order.<br><br>This only applies to purchases with a delivery service type.<br>|
|» » » address|body|object \| null|false|The postal address where the customer wants to receive the order.|
|» » » » administrativeArea|body|string \| null|false|Geographical region of this address. <br><br>Also known as County or State.<br><br>Required in Australia (AU) only for an order to be fulfilled.<br>|
|» » » » lines|body|[string]|false|One or more lines representing the street address.|
|» » » » locality|body|string \| null|false|The locality of this address.<br><br>Also known as Town or City.<br>|
|» » » » postalCode|body|string \| null|false|Postal code of this address.|
|» » » geolocation|body|object \| null|false|The coordinates of a geographical location where the customer wants to receive the order.<br><br>Required in Australia (AU) and New Zealand (NZ) only for an order to be fulfilled.<br>|
|» » » » latitude|body|number(decimal)|true|The latitude of the geographical location.|
|» » » » longitude|body|number(decimal)|true|The longitude of the geographical location.|
|» » time|body|object \| null|false|Time the customer wants to receive the order i.e. when order is fulfilled.|
|» » » asap|body|boolean|false|If the order should be fulfilled as soon as possible (ASAP).<br><br>ASAP may not be fulfillable.<br><br>Default is false.<br>|
|» » » scheduled|body|object \| null|false|Scheduled time the customer wants the order to be fulfilled.<br><br>The scheduled time will be ignored if ASAP is selected.<br>|
|» » » » from|body|string|true|Earliest time the customer wants the order to be fulfilled represented in ISO 8601 UTC (Zulu Time).|
|» » » » to|body|string|true|Latest time the customer wants the order to be fulfilled represented in ISO 8601 UTC (Zulu Time). <br><br>This time must be greater than or equal to the from time.<br>|
|» notes|body|[object]|false|Instructions about the order that the customer wants to submit.|
|» » note|body|string|true|The contents of the note.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of note.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|delivery|

`GET /consumers/{tenant}`

Currently this operation only supports retrieving a count of consumer accounts given an email address.

<h3 id="get-consumers-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|tenant|path|string|true|The identifier for the tenant.|

|accountType|query|string|true|The account type of the consumer - currently only 'registered' accounts are supported.|
|count|query|string|true|Returns the number of consumers that matches the `emailAddress` and `accountType`. The query value should be empty, e.g. `/consumers/uk/?emailAddress=someone@email.com&accountType=registered&count`.|

## Create consumer

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/consumers/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "emailAddress": "consumer@just-eat.com",
    "firstName": "Bob",
    "lastName": "Smith",
    "password": "Pa55word",
    "registrationSource": "Native"
  }'
```

`POST /consumers/{tenant}`

Creates a consumer for the given tenant.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emailAddress": "consumer@just-eat.com",
  "firstName": "Bob",
  "lastName": "Smith",
  "password": "Pa55word",
  "registrationSource": "Native"
}
```

<h3 id="create-consumer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|The identifier for the tenant. The only supported tenants are `uk`, `au` and `nz`|
|body|body|[ConsumerCreate](#schemaconsumercreate)|true|none|
|» emailAddress|body|string(email)|true|The consumer's email address|
|» firstName|body|string|true|The consumer's first name|
|» lastName|body|string|true|The consumer's last name|
|» marketingPreferences|body|[consumerMarketingPreference](#schemaconsumermarketingpreference)|false|The selected marketing preferences for the consumer|
|» password|body|string|false|The consumer's password|
|» registrationSource|body|string|false|The registration source of the consumer. Australia and New Zealand only support Guest|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» registrationSource|Native|
|» registrationSource|Guest|

  "type": "otac"

<h1 id="just-eat-uk-deliveryfee">DeliveryFee</h1>

## Get restaurant delivery fees

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/delivery-fees/uk?restaurantIds=1%2C2%2C3%2C4&deliveryTime=2019-09-05T12%3A43%3A48.431Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /delivery-fees/{tenant}`

Retrieve delivery fees for many restaurants. Returns fees and minimum order values required for delivery orders.

<h3 id="get-restaurant-delivery-fees-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|Tenant containing the restaurants.|
|restaurantIds|query|[string]|true|Restaurant IDs which fees are requested for. e.g. `?restaurantIds=1,2,3,4`|
|deliveryTime|query|string(date-time)|true|Delivery date/time when fees are required (ISO8601 format).|
|zone|query|string|false|Postcode or other location name identifying the location to which delivery is required. For use when precise location is not available. This will be removed in future in favour of location.|
|latlong|query|[number(double)]|false|Point to which delivery is required (latitude, longitude). Supply this where possible as support for zone-only based lookups will be removed in future.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "restaurants": [
    {
      "bands": [
        {
          "fee": 250,
          "minimumAmount": 1000
        }
      ],
      "minimumOrderValue": 1000,
      "restaurantId": "1234"
    },
    {
      "bands": [
        {
          "fee": 100,
          "minimumAmount": 0
        }
      ],
      "minimumOrderValue": 0,
      "restaurantId": "5678"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-restaurant-delivery-fees-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not found|None|

<h3 id="get-restaurant-delivery-fees-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|restaurants|[[RestaurantDeliveryFees](#schemarestaurantdeliveryfees)]|false|none|Collection of restaurants for which delivery fees were found.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update order with driver at delivery address details

```bash
curl https://example.com/orders/string/deliverystate/atdeliveryaddress \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "TimeStampWithUtcOffset": "2018-03-10T14:45:28.7537228+00:00"
  }'
```

`PUT /orders/{orderId}/deliverystate/atdeliveryaddress`

<p>The _at delivery address_ callback should be sent when the driver thinks that they have arrived at the specified delivery address.</p><p>NB&semi; This callback should be distinct from the delivered callback, as Just Eat use this callback to understand how much time is spent locating the customer's address.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "TimeStampWithUtcOffset": "2018-03-10T14:45:28.7537228+00:00"
}
```

<h3 id="update-order-with-driver-at-delivery-address-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|orderId|path|string|true|Just Eat order identifier|
|body|body|[delivery-details](#schemadelivery-details)|true|none|
|» Location|body|[location](#schemalocation)|false|GeoLocation object containing latitude and longitude values.|
|» TimeStampWithUtcOffset|body|string(date-time)|false|This should represent the delivery detailed updated timestamp.|

<h3 id="update-order-with-driver-at-delivery-address-details-responses">Responses</h3>

|200|OK|OK|None|

curl https://example.com/orders/string/deliverystate/atrestaurant \
  -X PUT \

  -d '{
    "EtaAtDeliveryAddress": "2018-03-10T15:45:28.7537228+00:00",
    "Location": {
      "Accuracy": 12.814,
      "Heading": 357.10382,
      "Latitude": 51.51641,

`PUT /orders/{orderId}/deliverystate/atrestaurant`

The _at restaurant_ callback should be sent when the driver arrives at the restaurant and is ready to collect the order.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "EtaAtDeliveryAddress": "2018-03-10T15:45:28.7537228+00:00",
  "Location": {
    "Accuracy": 12.814,
    "Heading": 357.10382,
    "Latitude": 51.51641,
    "Longitude": -0.103198,
    "Speed": 8.68
  },
  "TimeStampWithUtcOffset": "2018-03-10T14:45:28.7537228+00:00"
}
```

<h3 id="update-order-with-driver-at-restaurant-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|orderId|path|string|true|Just Eat order identifier|
|body|body|[delivery-driver-details-with-eta](#schemadelivery-driver-details-with-eta)|true|none|
|» EtaAtDeliveryAddress|body|string(date-time)|false|This should represent the delivery partner's best guess at when the driver will arrive at the delivery address.|
|» Location|body|[location](#schemalocation)|false|GeoLocation object containing latitude and longitude values.|
|» TimeStampWithUtcOffset|body|string(date-time)|false|This should represent the Eta calculated timestamp.|

## Update the driver's estimated time to arrive at the Restaurant

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/orders/string/deliverystate/atrestauranteta \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "bestGuess": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "estimatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`PUT /orders/{orderId}/deliverystate/atrestauranteta`

<p>In the UK, this endpoint updates the estimated arrival time at the restaurant. This value can be overridden from other endpoints like <a href="https://uk.api.just-eat.io/docs#tag/Order-Delivery-API/paths/~1orders~1{orderId}~1deliverystate~1driverlocation/put">Driver Locations</a> </p> <p> This endpoint should be used to set initial at restaurant ETAs prior to driver assignment where available. The earlier a delivery partner is able to provide an estimate of when the driver will arrive at the restaurant the more likely it is that driver arrival and order preparation will be aligned. </p> <p> In other tenants (Not UK):Note that if set for a given order, this Eta will NOT be overridden by any other at restaurant ETAs provided in `DriverAssigned` or `DriverLocation` requests</p> <p>This value is significant since it informs when a restaurant is instructed to start preparing food. When the time remaining between current time and the estimated time of arrival becomes less than the restaurant's configured preparation time, food preparation is initiated</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bestGuess": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "estimatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-drivers-estimated-time-to-arrive-at-the-restaurant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|orderId|path|string|true|Just Eat order identifier|
|body|body|[eta-estimate](#schemaeta-estimate)|true|none|
|» bestGuess|body|string(date-time)|false|This should represent the delivery partner's best guess at when the driver will arrive at the restaurant.|
|» estimatedAt|body|string(date-time)|false|This is the time at which you are doing the estimation|

<h3 id="update-the-drivers-estimated-time-to-arrive-at-the-restaurant-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`PUT /orders/{orderId}/deliverystate/driverlocation`

<p>Just Eat requires all delivery partners to send regular driver location callbacks, that record the GPS location of the drivers assigned to each order</p><p>Partners should aim to supply this callback approximately every 10 seconds.</p><p>Please provide an up-to-date ETA for when the driver will reach the restaurant in this request - this value is significant since it informs when a restaurant is instructed to start preparing food - when the time remaining between current time and the estimated time of arrival becomes less than the restaurant's configured preparation time, food preparation is initiated</p><p>Note that at restaurant Eta provided in this request will NOT override any ETA set in the Driver At Restaurant Eta request</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "EtaAtDeliveryAddress": "2020-12-25T16:45:28.7537228+00:00",
  "EtaAtRestaurant": "2020-12-25T16:30:28.7537228+00:00",
  "Location": {
    "Accuracy": 12.814,
    "Heading": 357.10382,
    "Latitude": 51.51641,
    "Longitude": -0.103198,
    "Speed": 8.68
  },
  "TimeStampWithUtcOffset": "2020-12-25T15:45:28.7537228+00:00"
}
```

|» EtaAtDeliveryAddress|body|string(date-time)|false|This should represent the delivery partner's best guess at when the driver will arrive at the delivery address.|
|» EtaAtRestaurant|body|string(date-time)|false|This should represent the delivery partner's best guess at when the driver will arrive at the restaurant.|
|» Location|body|[location](#schemalocation)|false|GeoLocation object containing latitude and longitude values.|
|» TimeStampWithUtcOffset|body|string(date-time)|false|This should represent the location updated timestamp.|

|202|Accepted|Pool has been updated|Inline|

|404|Not Found|The pool could not be found|None|

    "friday": {

        }
      ]
    },

`PUT /delivery/pools/{deliveryPoolId}/hours`

Set the daily start and end times for a pool or set closed flag if the pool does not operate on that day. Start and end times for all days must be provided. Though the API accepts array of start and end times for each day, multiple start and end time for a day are not accepted. If the end time for a day is equal to or before start time, end time will be considered as time for the next day.

> Body parameter

  "friday": {
    "closed": false,
    "poolTimes": [
      {
        "endTime": "01:00",
        "startTime": "12:00"
      }
    ]
  },

      {

        "startTime": "13:00"
      }
    ]
  },

    "closed": false,
    "poolTimes": [
      {
        "endTime": "03:00",
        "startTime": "12:00"
      }
    ]

## Order ready for pickup

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/order-is-ready-for-pickup \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "Event": "Ready for pickup",
    "Timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`PUT /order-is-ready-for-pickup`

<p>The "Ready for pickup" event lets the delivery partner know that the food has been cooked and is now ready for collection up from the restaurant.</p><p>When this event is received, it is important that you let your driver know that the order should now be collected from inside the restaurant. For example, this driver notification could take the form of an in-app notification or an SMS message.</p><p>This communication is needed to support restaurants who are unable to accommodate drivers inside their premises, as it allows restaurants to notify drivers waiting outside that they should come inside to collect their order.</p><p>NB&semi; This event can be sent by the restaurant at any point after the order is accepted by the restaurant (for instance, this event may be sent before the driver has arrived at the restaurant).</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "Event": "Ready for pickup",
  "Timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="order-ready-for-pickup-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ready-for-pickup](#schemaready-for-pickup)|true|none|
|» Event|body|string|false|none|
|» Timestamp|body|string(date-time)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

      "message": "string"
    }
  ]

```

<h3 id="order-requires-delivery-acceptance-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|In the event of successful handling of the request, a 201 status code should be returned, indicating acknowledgement of transmission success.|None|
|default|Default|In the case that the order cannot be accepted, an appropriate HTTP status code, such as 400 (Bad request) or 500 (Internal server error) should be returned.  In addition to the HTTP status code, a specific reason code and explanatory message should be provided within the response body|Inline|

<h3 id="order-requires-delivery-acceptance-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|false|none|none|
|» code|string|false|none|<p>Each code should be selected from the following list of valid reasons.</p><table><tr><th>code</th><th>explanation</th></tr><tr><td>`outside_hours`</td><td>Delivery partner is closed and not accepting requests.</td></tr><tr><td>`too_busy`</td><td>Delivery partner does not have enough capacity to accept this request.</td></tr><tr><td>`too_far`</td><td>The customer is too far away from the restaurant, either by time or distance.</td></tr><tr><td>`not_supported`</td><td>Delivery partner is currently unable to deliver to the customer's location.</td></tr><tr><td>`bad_address`</td><td>The order contains an address that could not be processed or understood.</td></tr><tr><td>`bad_request`</td><td>The order format is invalid or the order contains required data or information that cannot be processed.</td></tr><tr><td>`restaurant_not_configured`</td><td>Delivery partner is not configured to accept requests for given restaurant.</td></tr><tr><td>`duplicate`</td><td>The request has already been processed before.</td></tr><tr><td>`other`</td><td>Any validation failure or unexpected error not covered by the above codes.</td></tr></table>|
|» message|string|false|none|<p>The accompanying message should, in each case, provide an explanation of the specific problem that was experienced.</p><br/><p>Please note that the accompanying explanatory text are part of the code is only intended as an explanation of each reason code - and should not be returned to us as the message.</p>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» code|outside_hours|
|» code|too_busy|
|» code|too_far|
|» code|not_supported|
|» code|bad_address|
|» code|bad_request|
|» code|restaurant_not_configured|
|» code|duplicate|
|» code|other|

    "fault": {
      "errors": [
        {
          "code": "123",
          "description": "Invalid variation: 15237d6c-c866-55da-9e61-b4f59dcab9ae - variations must be associated with at least one availability"

        {
          "code": "145",
          "description": "Invalid availability ID: menu-105369-availabilities - availability IDs must be integers"

  }'
```

`POST /menu-ingestion-complete`

Callback to confirm that an attempt to ingest a menu has completed either successfully or unsuccessfully

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "correlationId": "64bef5ee-7265-47f8-9aee-28bc74f00b13",
  "fault": {
    "errors": [
      {
        "code": "123",
        "description": "Invalid variation: 15237d6c-c866-55da-9e61-b4f59dcab9ae - variations must be associated with at least one availability"
      },
      {
        "code": "145",
        "description": "Invalid availability ID: menu-105369-availabilities - availability IDs must be integers"
      }
    ],
    "id": "70e307df-0156-4d3c-ab92-dd57a103350b"
  },
  "restaurantId": "123456",
  "result": "fail",
  "tenant": "uk",
  "timestamp": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="menu-ingestion-complete-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[menu-ingestion-complete](#schemamenu-ingestion-complete)|true|none|
|» correlationId|body|string|false|The ID of the execution which has been completed|
|» fault|body|object|false|Details of the fault which caused the menu ingestion to fail. This is only present if menu ingestion did not complete successfully|
|» » errors|body|[object]|false|Details of errors which caused the fault|
|» » » code|body|string|false|An alphanumeric code for the error|
|» » » description|body|string|false|A description of the error to help you resolve the issue|
|» » id|body|string|false|A unique ID for the fault|
|» restaurantId|body|string|false|The Just Eat restaurant ID|
|» result|body|string(enum)|false|The result of the menu ingestion process|
|» tenant|body|string(enum)|false|Country code for the market the restaurant is in|
|» timestamp|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO-8601 datetime at which the menu ingestion completed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» result|success|
|» result|fail|
|» tenant|au|
|» tenant|dk|
|» tenant|es|
|» tenant|ie|
|» tenant|it|
|» tenant|no|
|» tenant|uk|
|» tenant|nz|

<h3 id="menu-ingestion-complete-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`POST /order-ready-for-preparation-async`

This webhook will be invoked when we have determined that an order is ready for preparation. Upon receiving the request, you should perform any preparation-related activities, such as sending the order to the POS system / kitchen screen.
**NOTE:** This version of the webhook is asynchronous, and we expect a response in two parts:
  1. We expect an immediate `202` response from this webhook to denote that you have received the request;
  2. Following that, we expect an [async callback](#section/Async-Webhooks) - indicating either success or failure of the operation. The body for the async callbacks are as below:
  
  **Success callback**
  ```
  {
        "status": "Success",
        "message": "Order successfully sent to POS",
        "data": {}
  }
  ```
  **Failure callback**
  ```
  {
        "status": "Failure",
        "message": "{errorMessage}",   // e.g. "The POS is currently in use"
        "data": {}
  }
  ```

## Send to POS failed

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/send-to-pos-failed \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "OrderId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /send-to-pos-failed`

This webhook will be invoked if we experience an error or timeout in sending an order to the underlying POS / kitchen screen. When notified via this webhook, typically you will perform some form of alerting or backup flow (e.g. ask the operator to enter the order manually into the POS). NOTE: This message contains the `OrderId`, but not the full order. It is assumed that you have stored/cached the full order details earlier in the flow - e.g. via the [/order-ready-for-preparation](#/paths/~1order-ready-for-preparation-sync/post) webhook.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "OrderId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="send-to-pos-failed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[send-to-pos-failed](#schemasend-to-pos-failed)|true|none|
|» OrderId|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="send-to-pos-failed-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Respond with a 200 status code to indicate that you have received the notification.|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`PUT /orders/{orderId}/duedate`

curl https://example.com/orders/string/string/consumerqueries/lateordercompensation/restaurantresponse \

  }'

`POST /orders/{tenant}/{orderId}/consumerqueries/lateordercompensation/restaurantresponse`

If a customer has requested compensation for a late order, a restaurant response is given by calling this endpoint.

  "acceptedAmount": 500,
  "isAccepted": true,
  "orderId": "69rqfxyfze2gjzf5nusdcw"
}

We hope you enjoyed your food.|

<h1 id="just-eat-uk-restaurant-events-webhooks">Restaurant Events Webhooks</h1>

## Restaurant Offline Status

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/restaurant-offline-status \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "AllowRestaurantOverride": false,
    "IsOffline": true,
    "RestaurantId": "123456",
    "Tenant": "uk"
  }'
```

`PUT /restaurant-offline-status`

Callback to notify that a restaurant has been taken offline through an active Restaurant Event or there's been a change in whether the restaurant can override a previous offline status.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "AllowRestaurantOverride": false,
  "IsOffline": true,
  "RestaurantId": "123456",
  "Tenant": "uk"
}
```

<h3 id="restaurant-offline-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RestaurantOfflineStatus](#schemarestaurantofflinestatus)|true|none|
|» AllowRestaurantOverride|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether a restaurant should be allowed to reverse this offline status change through calls to the Restaurant Events endpoints.|
|» IsOffline|body|boolean|false|Represents the current offline status of the restaurant.|
|» RestaurantId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the restaurant that has their offline status changed.|
|» Tenant|body|string(enum)|false|The two letter country code for the market in which the restaurant operates.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» Tenant|au|
|» Tenant|dk|
|» Tenant|es|
|» Tenant|ie|
|» Tenant|it|
|» Tenant|no|
|» Tenant|uk|
|» Tenant|nz|

<h3 id="restaurant-offline-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

    {
      "etaAtRestaurant": 1,
      "restaurantId": "1"
    }
  ]'

Set the average amount of time it will take a driver to collect a new order from a restaurant.

    "restaurantId": "1"
  }

## Create or Update Restaurant Fees

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/restaurants/string/string/fees \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bagFee": {
      "description": "A charge for bags in delivery",
      "serviceTypes": {
        "collection": {
          "amount": 5
        },
        "default": {
          "amount": 0
        },
        "delivery": {
          "amount": 10
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /restaurants/{tenant}/{restaurantId}/fees`

Creates or Updates the fees for a restaurant in a particular tenant

> Body parameter

```json

  "bagFee": {
    "description": "A charge for bags in delivery",

## Get the latest version of the restaurant's full menu

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/restaurants/string/string/menu \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /restaurants/{tenant}/{restaurantId}/menu`

The endpoint will return a 301 redirect containing a URL that will grant access to the Menu file. The URL will only be available for a short period of time. The Menu file will be a single document containing the information that Just Eat has and uses to display the Menu on our customer clients. This will include a collection of items, a collection of Categories and a collection of Availabilities for when the items are available. Partners will be able to retrieve the Menu for any Restaurants that they currently manage.

<h3 id="get-the-latest-version-of-the-restaurants-full-menu-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|The tenant of the restaurant in which to put a menu|
|restaurantId|path|string|true|The restaurant identifier to associated with the menu|
|Authorization|header|string|true|Containing a partner issued API key e.g. Bearer ABCDE123456789|

<h3 id="get-the-latest-version-of-the-restaurants-full-menu-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|301|Moved Permanently|Temporary Redirect. The redirect will contain the signed URL that the client needs to access the resource|[Menu](#schemamenu)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request. We were unable to process the request due to data you sent us|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[ConsumerErrorResponse](#schemaconsumererrorresponse)|

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-menu-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|The tenant of the restaurant in which to put a menu|
|restaurantId|path|string|true|The restaurant identifier to associated with the menu|
|Authorization|header|string|true|Containing a partner issued API key e.g. `JE-API-KEY ABCDE123456789`|
|Content-Type|header|string|false|Used to denote the version of the menu payload within the body, will default to latest if not supplied e.g. application/=1.0|
|body|body|[Menu](#schemamenu)|false|Specification of the menu. This must be valid according to the rules described here: https://developers.just-eat.com/docs/pos-how-the-integration-works#validation-rules|
|» currency|body|string|false|The currency of the items on the menu in ISO 4217 format, i.e. GBP, EUR or AUD|
|» description|body|string|false|A top level description for the menu.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the restaurant.|
|» restaurantId|body|string|false|A unique identifier at tenant level for a given restaurant.|
|» availabilities|body|[[Availability](#schemaavailability)]|false|A set of availabilities that can later be referenced by individual menu items.|
|» categories|body|[[Category](#schemacategory)]|false|A set of categories that appear on the menu.|
|» items|body|[[MenuItem](#schemamenuitem)]|false|All of the menu items within the menu.|

## Submit a restaurant response for the claim

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/restaurants/string/string/customerclaims/string/restaurantresponse \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "decision": "PartiallyAccepted",
    "items": [
      {
        "decision": "Accepted",
        "id": "NJ7iYXNrZXRJdGVtLTM2NTc0GTk2LTMwNDY2LXMzOWJxb3hkb2V1cGR4OXc4ZXZvcnc1"
      },
      {
        "decision": "Rejected",
        "id": "NJ7iYXNrZXRJdGVtLTM2NTc0GTk2LTMwNDY2LXMzOWJxb3hkb2V1cGR4OXc4ZXZvcnc3"
      }
    ],
    "justification": {
      "comments": "The food was packed properly",
      "reason": "Other"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /restaurants/{tenant}/{restaurantId}/customerclaims/{id}/restaurantresponse`

Submit a restaurant response for the claim, where the restaurant can tell us if they accept or reject the claim

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "decision": "PartiallyAccepted",
  "items": [
    {
      "decision": "Accepted",
      "id": "NJ7iYXNrZXRJdGVtLTM2NTc0GTk2LTMwNDY2LXMzOWJxb3hkb2V1cGR4OXc4ZXZvcnc1"
    },
    {
      "decision": "Rejected",
      "id": "NJ7iYXNrZXRJdGVtLTM2NTc0GTk2LTMwNDY2LXMzOWJxb3hkb2V1cGR4OXc4ZXZvcnc3"
    }
  ],
  "justification": {
    "comments": "The food was packed properly",
    "reason": "Other"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-restaurant-response-for-the-claim-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|Two letter code indicating the tenant|
|restaurantId|path|string|true|Just Eat restaurant identifier|
|id|path|string|true|Claim identifier|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|Indicates the representation of the request body the client is sending (including version)|
|body|body|[OrderClaimRestaurantResponse](#schemaorderclaimrestaurantresponse)|false|Payload containing the response of the restaurant on the order claim|
|» decision|body|string|false|Decision on the claim|
|» items|body|[[ItemDecision](#schemaitemdecision)]|false|Decisions on the items of a claim|
|» justification|body|[Justification](#schemajustification)|false|Reasons why of the decision for the claim|

|» decision|Rejected|

## Add reason and comments to the response

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/restaurants/string/string/customerclaims/string/restaurantresponse/justification \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comments": "The food was packed properly",
    "reason": "Other"
  }'
```

`PUT /restaurants/{tenant}/{restaurantId}/customerclaims/{id}/restaurantresponse/justification`

Add reason and optional comments in case of rejection of order claim

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comments": "The food was packed properly",
  "reason": "Other"
}

|id|path|string|true|Claim identifier|

|body|body|[Justification](#schemajustification)|false|Payload containing the reason of rejection and optional comments|
|» comments|body|string \| null|false|Comment from the restaurant owner in case they rejected at least one of the items and want to type their own rejection reason|

<h1 id="just-eat-uk-restaurant-events">Restaurant Events</h1>

## Create Offline Event

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/string/restaurants/event/offline \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-JE-Requester: string' \
  -H 'X-JE-User-Role: System' \
  -d '{
    "allowRestaurantOverride": true,
    "duration": "1:00:00",
    "name": "Out of Chicken",
    "reason": "No more chicken in stock.",
    "restaurantIds": "12345",
    "startDate": "2020-01-16T09:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/{tenant}/restaurants/event/offline`

Creates an event for the specified restaurants that indicates a reason for those restaurants to be offline.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowRestaurantOverride": true,
  "duration": "1:00:00",
  "name": "Out of Chicken",
  "reason": "No more chicken in stock.",
  "restaurantIds": "12345",
  "startDate": "2020-01-16T09:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-offline-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|The identifier for the tenant|
|X-JE-Requester|header|string|true|Name of the user or system creating the event. Used for auditing purposes|
|X-JE-User-Role|header|[UserRole](#schemauserrole)|true|none|
|body|body|[OfflineRestaurantsRequestModel](#schemaofflinerestaurantsrequestmodel)|true|none|
|» allowRestaurantOverride|body|boolean|true|Whether a restaurant should be allowed to delete this event, regardless of who raised it.|
|» category|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** A free text category used to group multiple events. This field is not intended to be used by clients.|
|» duration|body|string|false|Either a timespan in the HH:mm format or `untilTomorrow` (this will be the next day at 4:30 am +/- 10 minutes local time). Note if both duration and `endDate` are specified duration takes precedence.|
|» endDate|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|ISO 8601 format of the end datetime of the offline event.|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|body|[LegacyTempOfflineStatus](#schemalegacytempofflinestatus)|false|<br>- `Unset` : Legacy value meaning online.<br>- `None` : Legacy value meaning online.<br>- `TempOffline` : The restaurant will go temporarily offline, typically for an undetermined amount of time (no end date).<br>- `ClosedToday` : The restaurant will closed for the day and the event will end the next morning.<br>- `ClosedDueToEvent` : The restaurant will go offline for an event (e.g. a holiday), these events will typically have an end time.<br>- `FailedJctConnection` : The restaurant will go offline due to the POS device losing connection.<br>- `NoTrOverride` : The restaurant will go offline for another reason that the restaurant cannot override.<br>- `IgnoredOrders` : The restaurant will go offline due to ignoring orders.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the offline event to be created.|
|» reason|body|string|true|The reason for creating the offline event.|
|» restaurantIds|body|string|true|A comma separated list of the IDs of the restaurants to include in the offline event. No limit to the number accepted by the endpoint, but unexpected behaviour mat occur at more than 500 IDs.|
|» startDate|body|string(date-time)|true|ISO 8601 format of the start datetime of the offline event.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|X-JE-User-Role|System|
|X-JE-User-Role|Operations|
|X-JE-User-Role|Restaurant|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|Unset|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|None|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|TempOffline|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|ClosedToday|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|ClosedDueToEvent|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|FailedJctConnection|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|NoTrOverride|
|» legacyTempOfflineType|IgnoredOrders|

  "restaurantIds": "12345"
}

## Delete Offline Event

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/string/restaurants/string/event/offline \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'X-JE-Requester: string' \
  -H 'X-JE-User-Role: System'
```

`DELETE /v1/{tenant}/restaurants/{id}/event/offline`

Removes specified restaurant from offline events. If role header is `System` or `Operations` only events created by the specified role will be affected. If role header is `Restaurant` then all events that have `allowRestaurantOverride=true` will be affected.

<h3 id="delete-offline-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|The identifier for the tenant|
|id|path|string|true|The identifier for the restaurant|
|X-JE-Requester|header|string|true|Name of the user or system creating the event. Used for auditing purposes|
|X-JE-User-Role|header|[UserRole](#schemauserrole)|true|The role the user or system creating the event has assumed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|X-JE-User-Role|System|
|X-JE-User-Role|Operations|
|X-JE-User-Role|Restaurant|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
[
  {
    "attemptedValue": null,
    "customState": null,
    "errorCode": "NotEmptyValidator",
    "errorMessage": "TestProperty is empty",
    "formattedMessageArguments": [],
    "formattedMessagePlaceHolderValues": {
      "PropertyName": "User Role",
      "PropertyValue": null
    },
    "propertyName": "TestProperty",
    "resourceName": null,
    "severity": 0
  }
]
```

<h3 id="delete-offline-event-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|No Events to Delete|None|
|202|Accepted|Request Succeeded|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|None|

<h3 id="delete-offline-event-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[ValidationError](#schemavalidationerror)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="just-eat-uk-attempted-delivery-api">Attempted Delivery API</h1>

## Delivery Attempt Failed

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/string/orders/string/queries/attempteddelivery \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ReasonCode": "problem_with_address"
  }'
```

`POST /{tenant}/orders/{orderId}/queries/attempteddelivery`

If the customer hasn't answered the door to collect the order, then an attempted delivery event can be created using this endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ReasonCode": "problem_with_address"
}
```

<h3 id="delivery-attempt-failed-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|Request tenant e.g. uk.|
|orderId|path|string|true|Id for the order.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|Containing a partner issued API key e.g. `JE-API-KEY ABCDE123456789`|
|body|body|[create-attempted-delivery](#schemacreate-attempted-delivery)|true|An object for providing the reason that the attempted delivery event is being created|
|» ReasonCode|body|string|false|The reason the attempted delivery event was created|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ReasonCode|problem_with_address|
|» ReasonCode|no_answer|

<h3 id="delivery-attempt-failed-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request - returned if providing invalid data such as an unacceptable reason code|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - consumer has not provided the necessary credentials|None|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Request Redelivery of the Order

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/string/orders/string/queries/attempteddelivery/resolution/redeliverorder \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "NewDueDate": "2018-03-10T14:45:28Z",
    "Status": "driver_at_address"
  }'
```

`POST /{tenant}/orders/{orderId}/queries/attempteddelivery/resolution/redeliverorder`

If the customer responds, then you can trigger the redelivery of an order through this endpoint

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "NewDueDate": "2018-03-10T14:45:28Z",
  "Status": "driver_at_address"
}
```

<h3 id="request-redelivery-of-the-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tenant|path|string|true|Request tenant e.g. uk.|
|orderId|path|string|true|Id for the order.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|Containing a partner issued API key e.g. `JE-API-KEY ABCDE123456789`|
|body|body|[resolve-attempted-delivery-redeliver](#schemaresolve-attempted-delivery-redeliver)|true|An object for providing the new status of the order and the updated due date|
|» NewDueDate|body|string(date-time)|false|Updated due date for delivery of the order|
|» Status|body|string|false|The current status of the order|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» Status|driver_at_address|
|» Status|repreparing|

<h3 id="request-redelivery-of-the-order-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request - returned if providing invalid data such as an unacceptable reason code|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - consumer has not provided the necessary credentials|None|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h2 id="tocS_BenderFlexStateType">BenderFlexStateType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabenderflexstatetype"></a>
<a id="schema_BenderFlexStateType"></a>
<a id="tocSbenderflexstatetype"></a>
<a id="tocsbenderflexstatetype"></a>

```json
"CODE_RED"
```

<p>The flex state type changes according to the exponential moving average and is used as a reference to bring more couriers to suffice the demand in a given delivery zone.</p> <p>If the flex state type is "Off", it means no shifts will be offered for the delivery zone.</p> <p>If the state is "CLOSED", only scheduled shifts will be allowed for the delivery zone.</p> <p>If the state is "SEEKING", the shift offers are going to be made across the courier network in order to suffice the current demand.</p> <p>If the state is "OPEN", it means demand is high and couriers from all over the courier network are allowed to create shifts for themselves to suffice the current demand.</p> <p>If the state is "CODE_RED", it means not only can everyone create shifts for themselves for the delivery zone but also couriers from other delivery zones might reallocate to help suffice the demand of that particular delivery zone.</p>

<h2 id="tocS_BonusType">BonusType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabonustype"></a>
<a id="schema_BonusType"></a>
<a id="tocSbonustype"></a>
<a id="tocsbonustype"></a>

```json
"TOP_UP_PROMOTION"
```

Types of bonuses that may be granted to the courier. <p>TOP_UP_PROMOTION - In order to calculate top up promotion skip has a database table containing required acceptance rate and top up value for each existing delivery zone, when the courier's order acceptance rate is greater than the required acceptance rate and the total value is lower than top up value for that given delivery zone, the courier will be granted the difference between the top up value and total order value, know as top up promotion.</p>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acr_values|string|false|none|Allows passing in additional authentication related information for the `password` grant type - the following  are special proprietary `acr_values`:<br>- `idp:name_of_idp` bypasses the login/home realm screen and forwards the user directly to the selected identity provider (if allowed per client configuration)<br>- `tenant:name_of_tenant` can be used to pass a tenant name to the token endpoint|
|client_id|string|true|none|client identifier|
|client_secret|string|false|none|The client secret - either in the post body, or as a basic authentication header.|
|code|string|false|none|The authorization code (required for `authorization_code` grant type)|
|code_verifier|string|false|none|PKCE proof key|
|device_code|string|false|none|The device code (required for `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` grant type)|
|grant_type|string|true|none|The grant type which determines the type of flow. A custom value is also allowed.|
|password|string|false|none|Resource owner password (required for `password` grant type)|
|redirect_uri|string|false|none|Required for the `authorization_code` grant type|
|refresh_token|string|false|none|The refresh token (required for `refresh_token` grant type)|
|scope|string|false|none|One or more registered scopes. If not specified, a token for all explicitly  allowed scopes will be issued.|
|username|string|false|none|Resource owner username (required for `password` grant type)|

<h2 id="tocS_CourierStatus">CourierStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacourierstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_CourierStatus"></a>
<a id="tocScourierstatus"></a>
<a id="tocscourierstatus"></a>

```json
"ONBOARDING"
```

The courier application status. A courier could have one of these status associated with their application, here is a brief example of each status. <p>`ON-BOARDING` - Courier is actively trying to be on-boarded and will progress through the courier on-boarding program</p><p>`STALLED` - Courier has not proceeded with a step inside the courier on-boarding program for 14 days and will not to proceed further</p><p>`SURPLUS` - Zone has been closed for On-boarding; courier cannot proceed until zone on-boarding re-opens</p><p>`ACTIVE` - Courier has interacted with the app within the last two weeks and will be automatically scheduled based on their availability, receive notifications and may complete orders</p><p>`INACTIVE` - Courier has not interacted with the app for at least two weeks, and will not be scheduled for shifts. May interact with the app to convert their status to active, and be eligible for shifts and deliveries</p><p>`RELIABILITY_ISSUES` - No longer in use, historically account was suspended due to frequent flakes or rejected orders</p><p>`VEHICLE_ISSUES` - Account suspended due to reported vehicle problems, but may reactivate by contacting courier support</p><p>`INCIDENT_ISSUES` - Account suspended indefinitely due to significant concern (used exclusively by Incidents team)</p><p>`OTHER_ACCOUNT_ISSUES` - General account suspension, usually in connection with problems not categorised under regular courier status</p><p>`EXPIRED_DOCUMENTS` - General account suspension, typically for expired right to work documentation</p><p>`REJECTED` - Applicant did not meet minimum requirements for access to the network</p><p>`WITHDRAWN` - Applicant decided not to proceed with onboarding</p><p>`BANNED` - Courier’s access to the network was revoked following escalation</p><p>`LEFT_NETWORK` - Courier voluntarily left the network</p>

The courier zone flex state object, contains the flex state type and the flex availability status for a given delivery zone.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|deliveryZoneId|string|false|none|Delivery zone identifier for flex state.|
|deliveryZoneName|string|false|none|Delivery zone name for flex state.|
|flexAvailable|boolean|false|none|Flex states are enabled when true|
|flexStateType|[SyncFlexStateType](#schemasyncflexstatetype)|false|none|<p>The flex state type changes according to the exponential moving average and is used as a reference to bring more couriers to suffice the demand in a given delivery zone.</p> <p>If the flex state type is "Off", it means no shifts will be offered for the delivery zone.</p> <p>If the state is "CLOSED", only scheduled shifts will be allowed for the delivery zone.</p> <p>If the state is "SEEKING", the shift offers are going to be made across the courier network in order to suffice the current demand.</p> <p>If the state is "OPEN", it means demand is high and couriers from all over the courier network are allowed to create shifts for themselves to suffice the current demand.</p> <p>If the state is "CODE_RED", it means not only can everyone create shifts for themselves for the delivery zone but also couriers from other delivery zones might reallocate to help suffice the demand of that particular delivery zone.</p>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|flexStateType|CODE_RED|
|flexStateType|OPEN|
|flexStateType|SEEKING|
|flexStateType|CLOSED|

The job type classifies the type of job assigned to the courier. When an order is placed by the customer, two jobs are created for the courier, a collect job and a deliver job, basically the courier have to complete both jobs, first the collect job, which is the one where the order is collected from the restaurant and the deliver job as the job of delivering the order to the customer.

<h2 id="tocS_LegacyTempOfflineStatus">LegacyTempOfflineStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalegacytempofflinestatus"></a>
<a id="schema_LegacyTempOfflineStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSlegacytempofflinestatus"></a>
<a id="tocslegacytempofflinestatus"></a>

```json
"ClosedDueToEvent"
```


- `Unset` : Legacy value meaning online.
- `None` : Legacy value meaning online.
- `TempOffline` : The restaurant will go temporarily offline, typically for an undetermined amount of time (no end date).
- `ClosedToday` : The restaurant will closed for the day and the event will end the next morning.
- `ClosedDueToEvent` : The restaurant will go offline for an event (e.g. a holiday), these events will typically have an end time.
- `FailedJctConnection` : The restaurant will go offline due to the POS device losing connection.
- `NoTrOverride` : The restaurant will go offline for another reason that the restaurant cannot override.
- `IgnoredOrders` : The restaurant will go offline due to ignoring orders.

|categories|[[Category](#schemacategory)]|false|none|A set of categories that appear on the menu.|
|items|[[MenuItem](#schemamenuitem)]|false|none|All of the menu items within the menu.|

<h2 id="tocS_OfflineRestaurantsRequestModel">OfflineRestaurantsRequestModel</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaofflinerestaurantsrequestmodel"></a>
<a id="schema_OfflineRestaurantsRequestModel"></a>
<a id="tocSofflinerestaurantsrequestmodel"></a>
<a id="tocsofflinerestaurantsrequestmodel"></a>

```json
{
  "allowRestaurantOverride": true,
  "duration": "1:00:00",
  "name": "Out of Chicken",
  "reason": "No more chicken in stock.",
  "restaurantIds": "12345",
  "startDate": "2020-01-16T09:00:00Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowRestaurantOverride|boolean|true|none|Whether a restaurant should be allowed to delete this event, regardless of who raised it.|
|category|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** A free text category used to group multiple events. This field is not intended to be used by clients.|
|duration|string|false|none|Either a timespan in the HH:mm format or `untilTomorrow` (this will be the next day at 4:30 am +/- 10 minutes local time). Note if both duration and `endDate` are specified duration takes precedence.|
|endDate|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 format of the end datetime of the offline event.|
|legacyTempOfflineType|[LegacyTempOfflineStatus](#schemalegacytempofflinestatus)|false|none|<br>- `Unset` : Legacy value meaning online.<br>- `None` : Legacy value meaning online.<br>- `TempOffline` : The restaurant will go temporarily offline, typically for an undetermined amount of time (no end date).<br>- `ClosedToday` : The restaurant will closed for the day and the event will end the next morning.<br>- `ClosedDueToEvent` : The restaurant will go offline for an event (e.g. a holiday), these events will typically have an end time.<br>- `FailedJctConnection` : The restaurant will go offline due to the POS device losing connection.<br>- `NoTrOverride` : The restaurant will go offline for another reason that the restaurant cannot override.<br>- `IgnoredOrders` : The restaurant will go offline due to ignoring orders.|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the offline event to be created.|
|reason|string|true|none|The reason for creating the offline event.|
|restaurantIds|string|true|none|A comma separated list of the IDs of the restaurants to include in the offline event. No limit to the number accepted by the endpoint, but unexpected behaviour mat occur at more than 500 IDs.|
|startDate|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO 8601 format of the start datetime of the offline event.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|legacyTempOfflineType|Unset|
|legacyTempOfflineType|None|
|legacyTempOfflineType|TempOffline|
|legacyTempOfflineType|ClosedToday|
|legacyTempOfflineType|ClosedDueToEvent|
|legacyTempOfflineType|FailedJctConnection|
|legacyTempOfflineType|NoTrOverride|
|legacyTempOfflineType|IgnoredOrders|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acceptedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time order was accepted by the restaurant|
|acceptedFor|string(date-time)|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time time due at the point of acceptance|
|addressLines|[string]|false|none|Customer address|
|asSoonAsPossible|boolean|false|none|Will be false if order was a preorder|
|attemptedDeliveryQuery|[AttemptedDeliveryQuery](#schemaattempteddeliveryquery)|false|none|Details of any attempted delivery query attached to the order|
|badItemClaims|[[BadItemClaim](#schemabaditemclaim)]|false|none|A list of bad item claims attached to the order|
|cancellationInfo|[CancellationInfo](#schemacancellationinfo)|false|none|Details of any cancellation attached to the order|
|cancelledAt|string(date-time)|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time order was cancelled|
|city|string \| null|false|none|Customer city|
|customerId|string \| null|false|none|Platform customer id|
|customerNote|string \| null|false|none|Customer added notes|
|deliveredAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time order was delivered|
|deliveryDriverInfo|[DeliveryDriverInfo](#schemadeliverydriverinfo)|false|none|Delivery driver information|
|deliveryDriverUsername|string \| null|false|none|Delivery drivers user name (usually their phone number)|
|deliveryNote|string \| null|false|none|Delivery specific notes|
|eposState|[EposState](#schemaeposstate)|false|none|Current state of sending the order to the restaurants EPOS system|
|estimatedDeliveryTimeInSeconds|integer(int32)|false|none|How long until order will be delivered in seconds (RDS only)|
|estimatedHandoverTimeInSeconds|integer(int32)|false|none|How long until order needs to be handed over to driver in seconds (RDS only)|
|externalCustomerId|string \| null|false|none|Customer id restaurants can use to identify customer|
|id|string \| null|false|none|Id used to identify the order in Zeus|
|isPreorder|boolean|false|none|Whether order is a preorder|
|isRdsOrder|boolean|false|none|Will be true if delivery is being arranged by Just Eat|
|lateOrderCompensationQuery|[LateOrderCompensationQuery](#schemalateordercompensationquery)|false|none|Details of any late order compensation query attached to the order|
|lateOrderInfo|[LateOrderInfo](#schemalateorderinfo)|false|none|Details of any late order query attached to the order|
|location|[GeoLocation](#schemageolocation)|false|none|Geo location of the customers address|
|missingItemClaims|[[MissingItemClaim](#schemamissingitemclaim)]|false|none|A list of missing item claims attached to the order|
|modernId|string \| null|false|none|Just Eat modern order id|
|name|string \| null|false|none|Customer name|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|General order notes|
|orderHistory|[[OrderHistoryItem](#schemaorderhistoryitem)]|false|none|Ordered history of status updates to the order and when they happened|
|orderItems|[[OrderItem](#schemaorderitem)]|false|none|A list of order items|
|orderState|[ClientOrderState](#schemaclientorderstate)|false|none|Current state of the order|
|orderType|[OrderType](#schemaordertype)|false|none|Type of order (collection or delivery)|
|paymentInfo|[PaymentInfo](#schemapaymentinfo)|false|none|Payment details for the order|
|phone|string \| null|false|none|Customer phone number (will be phone masking number in markets when enabled)|
|phoneMaskingCode|string \| null|false|none|Code to use when calling customer phone masking number about this order|
|postcode|string \| null|false|none|Customer postcode|
|preferredTimeDue|string(date-time)|false|none|Current agreed delivery time of the order|
|prepareOrderFor|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time when order should be prepared for|
|previousOrders|string \| null|false|none|Number of previous Just Eat orders by the customer|
|previousOrdersToRestaurant|string \| null|false|none|Number of previous orders by the customer to this restaurant|
|rdsPickupTime|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time when order will be picked up by RDS partner|
|receivedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time order was paid|
|restaurantId|string \| null|false|none|Restaurant Id of the order|
|restaurantInformation|[RestaurantInfo](#schemarestaurantinfo)|false|none|Restaurant information for the order|
|sourcePartner|[PartnerInfo](#schemapartnerinfo)|false|none|Information about the source of the order (Just Eat, Third Party etc.)|
|startOrderPreparationAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time for restaurant to start preparing the order|
|timeDue|string(date-time)|false|none|Current agreed delivery time of the order|
|withDriverAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 Date/Time order was handed over to driver|

<h2 id="tocS_SyncFlexStateType">SyncFlexStateType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasyncflexstatetype"></a>
<a id="schema_SyncFlexStateType"></a>
<a id="tocSsyncflexstatetype"></a>
<a id="tocssyncflexstatetype"></a>

```json
"CODE_RED"
```

<p>The flex state type changes according to the exponential moving average and is used as a reference to bring more couriers to suffice the demand in a given delivery zone.</p> <p>If the flex state type is "Off", it means no shifts will be offered for the delivery zone.</p> <p>If the state is "CLOSED", only scheduled shifts will be allowed for the delivery zone.</p> <p>If the state is "SEEKING", the shift offers are going to be made across the courier network in order to suffice the current demand.</p> <p>If the state is "OPEN", it means demand is high and couriers from all over the courier network are allowed to create shifts for themselves to suffice the current demand.</p> <p>If the state is "CODE_RED", it means not only can everyone create shifts for themselves for the delivery zone but also couriers from other delivery zones might reallocate to help suffice the demand of that particular delivery zone.</p>

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaupdateorderaddressrequest"></a>

<a id="tocSupdateorderaddressrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsupdateorderaddressrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "address": [
    "123 Wye Avenue, Eaton"
  ],
  "city": "Bristol",
  "email": "user@email.com",
  "geoPosition": {
    "latitude": 456.123,
    "longitude": 123.456
  },
  "name": "J.E.Hungerton",
  "orderable": true,
  "phoneNumber": "0123456789",
  "polygonName": "BS1 1AA",
  "postCode": "BS1 1AA",
  "serviceType": "delivery"
}
```

The request object for setting the order address of a basket.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|[string]|true|none|An array of strings containing lines of the customer's order address.|
|city|string|true|none|String value containing the city name of the customer's order address.|
|email|string|true|none|The customer's email address.|
|geoPosition|object \| null|true|none|Geoposition object containing latitude and longitude values for the customer's order address|
|name|string|false|none|The customer's name.|
|phoneNumber|string|true|none|The customer's phone number.|
|polygonName|string|true|none|String value containing the polygon name of customer's order address (in tenants with no polygon name, will be the same as postcode).|
|postCode|string|true|none|String value containing the postcode of the customer's order address.|
|serviceType|string|false|none|Service Type associated with the order details.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|serviceType|delivery|
|serviceType|collection|

<h2 id="tocS_Variation">Variation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavariation"></a>
<a id="schema_Variation"></a>
<a id="tocSvariation"></a>
<a id="tocsvariation"></a>

```json
{
  "availabilityIds": [
    "1-lunch-delivery",
    "2-lunch-collection",
    "3-dinner-delivery",
    "4-dinner-collection"
  ],
  "basePrice": 1000,
  "dealGroupsIds": [],
  "dealOnly": false,
  "id": "8547130",
  "kitchenNumber": "100",
  "modifierGroupsIds": [
    "8547130-req-1",
    "8547130-opt-1"
  ],
  "name": "12 inch",
  "type": "variation"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|availabilityIds|[string]|false|none|Maps to an availability item, availabilities determines which days and times the item can be sold.|
|basePrice|number(int32)|false|none|The base price of this variation in the minor unit of the currency.|
|dealGroupsIds|[string]|false|none|Maps to the deal groups that are applicable to this variation.|
|dealOnly|boolean|false|none|This flag indicates the variation is only available as part of a deal, the item will not be displayed as a stand alone menu item.|
|id|string|false|none|A unique identifier at menu level for a variation, can be shared with parent menu item id.|
|kitchenNumber|string|false|none|Identifies the item with a number on the physical menu that the kitchen understand e.g. on a Chinese menu number 16 could correspond to "BBQ ribs"|
|modifierGroupsIds|[string]|false|none|Maps to the modifier groups that are applicable to this variation.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the variation.|
|type|string|false|none|Denotes the type of variation, `Variation` if there's multiple variations of the parent `menuitem`, `NoVariation` if there's only one|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|noVariation|
|type|variation|

<h2 id="tocS_ZoneProfile">ZoneProfile</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemazoneprofile"></a>
<a id="schema_ZoneProfile"></a>
<a id="tocSzoneprofile"></a>
<a id="tocszoneprofile"></a>

```json
{
  "averageAssignableJobLoad": 0.7,
  "bender": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "ema": 70,
  "flexStateType": "CODE_RED",
  "zoneId": "53c3afb5-fcs5-4941-be6d-2179f812sc8d"
}
```

The zone profile object for a given delivery zone.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|averageAssignableJobLoad|number(double)|false|none|The burden over the couriers in a delivery zone. The average assignable job load is calculated by the sum of all jobs assigned to the couriers divided by the delivery zone's total assignable courier count.|
|bender|object|false|none|Bender On/Off object|
|ema|number(integer)|false|none|The simple moving average is the usage for a given delivery zone, which is calculated by using the sum of all on-shift utilisation ( percentage of time a courier spends working on orders during their shift ) at the time, divided by the number of time periods gathered from all data points. Differently from simple moving average, exponential moving average also represents the usage however its equation places a greater weight on the most recent data points.|
|flexStateType|[BenderFlexStateType](#schemabenderflexstatetype)|false|none|The flex state type changes according to the exponential moving average and is used as a reference to bring more couriers to suffice the demand in a given delivery zone.|
|zoneId|string|false|none|Zone profile delivery zone id.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|flexStateType|CODE_RED|
|flexStateType|OPEN|
|flexStateType|SEEKING|
|flexStateType|CLOSED|
|flexStateType|Off|

  "correlationId": "64bef5ee-7265-47f8-9aee-28bc74f00b13",
  "fault": {
    "errors": [
      {
        "code": "123",
        "description": "Invalid variation: 15237d6c-c866-55da-9e61-b4f59dcab9ae - variations must be associated with at least one availability"
      },
      {
        "code": "145",
        "description": "Invalid availability ID: menu-105369-availabilities - availability IDs must be integers"
      }
    ],
    "id": "70e307df-0156-4d3c-ab92-dd57a103350b"
  },
  "restaurantId": "123456",
  "result": "fail",
  "tenant": "uk",
  "timestamp": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|correlationId|string|false|none|The ID of the execution which has been completed|
|fault|object|false|none|Details of the fault which caused the menu ingestion to fail. This is only present if menu ingestion did not complete successfully|
|restaurantId|string|false|none|The Just Eat restaurant ID|
|result|string(enum)|false|none|The result of the menu ingestion process|
|tenant|string(enum)|false|none|Country code for the market the restaurant is in|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|false|none|The ISO-8601 datetime at which the menu ingestion completed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|result|success|
|result|fail|
|tenant|au|
|tenant|dk|
|tenant|es|
|tenant|ie|
|tenant|it|
|tenant|no|
|tenant|uk|
|tenant|nz|
